title: Extremal $t$-intersecting Families of Permutations for Large $t$
summary: A set of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ is $t$-intersecting if any two permutations agree on at least $t$ inputs. A recent work by Kupavskii, in the spirit of the Erdős-Ko-Rado Theorem, shows that for all $t\leq n-O\left(\frac{n\log\log n}{\log n}\right)$, every $t$-intersecting family of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ with the maximum size must be isomorphic to the set $$A_k = \{σ: σ(i)=i\text{ for at least } t+k \text{ indices } i\in\{1,2,\dots,t+2k\}\}$$ for some $k$.
